assignments.note: 2026-07 Stop Guessing When to Stop Testing
assignments.why: Group sequential testing with Pocock boundaries that stops a benchmark run once a CI, gap or threshold goal is met with valid error control.
A meta-evaluation benchmark measuring LLM judges' alignment ceiling (audits) built from 3,808 agentic tool-calling workflow instances across DAG topologies (agent evaluation benchmarks).
Empirical measurement of an anchoring bias in LLM judges from prior scores in metadata, with CoT and warnings failing to remove it.

assignments.note: 2026-08 Benchmarking LLM Judges for Mobile Agent Evaluation
assignments.why: MobileJudgeBench meta-evaluates six judge methods by five backends with their failure profiles (audits) on 931 human-annotated mobile-agent trajectories (agent evaluation benchmarks).
Bayesian optimal stopping that ends item- and group-level sampling once a hierarchical credible interval is narrow enough.

Reads Jev-style typed decisions from one prefill of any open LLM (decision models) as a training-free recipe from an existing LLM (open decision models), with cyclic rotations and label-prior division removing position and label bias (presentation sensitivity).
Measures whether Jev's probabilities obey the probability axioms against an open LLM (decision model, audit), with probabilistic coherence as the subject (calibration).

An open encoder-decoder System One decision model released with its training recipe, whose outcome-learning stage is argued to converge to true probabilities via the Brier gradient and is judged on ECE/NLL (calibration).

Independent audit of Jev coding crash narratives, with Platt recalibration and a resolution-floor result (calibration) and calibrated probabilities turned into a human-review budget for records that cannot be auto-accepted (escalation to humans).
A 322M Chinese Jev-style decision model trained and released (open decision models) with a proper-scoring-rule RLCD term aimed at calibrated distributions and ECE as a headline result (calibration).

assignments.note: 2026-09 Decision Models vs LLMs as Rubric Judges
assignments.why: Compares Jev and Decider against LLM rubric judges and measures their correlated errors (audits), centred on whether a decision-model-first confidence-gated cascade can beat its fallback (escalation).

assignments.note: 2026-09 Do System One Decisions Add Up
assignments.why: Measures Jev and Laya's coherence across parent, fine and conditional label questions (audit of decision models), probabilistic coherence being the subject (calibration).
Adds a native typed-decision action head to a pretrained open LLM and trains it with alignment plus RL, a recipe for building a System One decision capability from an existing LLM.

assignments.note: 2026-09 Evaluating and Benchmarking the System One Model Jev
assignments.why: Independent 37-dataset evaluation of Jev against open LLMs (audit of a decision model) that tests the vendor's calibration claim with ECE and threshold analysis (calibration).
PixelJev puts a Jev-style decision contract on open VLMs and studies few-shot LoRA adaptation of it, a recipe for an open visual decision model.
An offline protocol measuring when LLM-judge rankings of agents fail to track grounded task success (audit) in user-simulated conversations on tau2-bench and SimulatorArena (user simulation).

assignments.note: 2026-09 JEV as a Judge for Agent Trace Security
assignments.why: Empirical comparison of the typed decision model JEV with four generative LLM judges on labelling agent traces safe or unsafe, measuring F1, precision/recall balance, cost and latency.
A decision-only Jev judge design (decision model used as judge) that accepts when confident and escalates low-confidence cases to a reasoning judge (escalation).

assignments.note: 2026-09 Jev Thinks I Dont Know Sys1Cal-v1
assignments.why: A benchmark with exactly known probabilities measuring Jev's three primitives (audit) and an inverse map that recalibrates its Choice outputs (calibration).
A census of 2,170 GitHub projects built on the Jev decision model, mapping its interfaces and the roles it plays inside pipelines and agents.
Uses jev-1.13.0 as a RAG claim-verification judge against a frontier LLM judge, with a cross-fitted cheap-first confidence-gated cascade as the central method.
Fine-tunes open LLMs/VLMs to answer typed decisions with one shuffled control token in one decode step, a recipe for a single-pass decision model from an existing LLM.
Extends the open Laya encoder with a trained value-of-information head (open decision model) so it decides whether to ask a clarifying question, decide or hand off (abstention and fallback).

Reports 11 failure modes of LLM judges inside self-improving agent loops (audit), proposes deterministic acceptance checks, holdouts and canaries that outrank the judge (non-single-judge evaluation), and documents reward hacking when the judge drives the improvement loop (judges as reward signals).

assignments.note: 2026-09 Laya as a Typed Probabilistic Assessor
assignments.why: Preregistered reproduction of the Laya decision model (audit) that measures its under-confidence and fixes it with one temperature (calibration) and tests its accept-or-escalate gate against a 10% error target (escalation).

Measures ordinal-scale compression in JEV, KEV and StartLux (audit of decision models), showing verdicts change with how finely the listed scale is refined and with candidate order (presentation sensitivity).
A 233-task deployment-aware agent benchmark in one shared runtime (agent evaluation benchmarks) with a meta-judge auditing the first judge's positive scores (judge-the-judge).
An open recipe for training Jev-like calibrated decision readouts (open decision models) by scoring per-rationale readouts with strictly proper scoring rules (calibration).

A fine-tuning recipe for single-token typed-decision models (open decision models) whose permutation-consistency term targets position bias (presentation sensitivity) and whose choice-count- and length-conditioned serving temperature targets calibration.

Benchmarks Jev, Kev and Qwen probability reports against exact posteriors (audit) on accuracy and coherence identities (calibration), showing equivalent interfaces and option orders change act-or-defer decisions (presentation sensitivity).
